::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Aug 9th [1889?]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Columbia University Library, New York:  Samuels, J.H. Collection
:::

My dear [Fanny](people/person_1151.qmd)

[Mrs Selwyn](people/person_1297.qmd) comes on Thursday, the [Bishop](people/person_1296.qmd) on Saturday.[^1] It will be a very thing if you do go down to enliven Mrs Selwyn on Friday for it has so turned out that this week is the only one when I can go down to see my poor dear old [May](people/person_351.qmd), so I am going down there from Tuesday till Friday evening or Saturday morning I am not sure which. I am sorry to miss you but I dare say you will be about again  and poor May wants me. [Alice](people/person_327.qmd) will be there the last day I think.

If you do come down on Friday, and it is not a bad day with [Gertrude](people/person_1462.qmd), she will be delighted to see you for a little while - the best time between 3 and 4 or 5

Your affte cousin
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The Rt. Rev. John Richardson Selwyn  (1844-1898), who became Bishop of Melanesia in 1877 and retired  to England finally in September 1891.  This letter may date however from his previous visit to England in June 1889-January 1890.  The Mrs Selwyn referred to is probably his mother, Sarah Harriet Richardson (d. 1907), widow of the Rt. Rev. George Augustus Selwyn (1809-1878), bishop of New |Zealand and then of Lichfield, though it appears that his second wife Annie Catherine (Mort) Selwyn, whom he had married in 1885. was also present.
